card.name: Palo (Baile de palo)
card.era: Colonial roots (16th c.); continuous folk-religious practice
card.tagline: Afro-Dominican sacred drum-and-dance for saints and misterios.
card.profile: Palo (also atabales; baile de palos as the dance) is Afro-Dominican sacred drum-and-dance music with roots in the Kongo region of Central-West Africa, played at religious ceremonies coinciding with saints' days (velaciones), funerals and special occasions. Drums called palos are hollowed logs with cowhide heads: a master drum (palo mayor) with two or three slimmer alcahuetes, plus guira. Palos are tied to Dominican folk Catholicism and the cofradias, with a pantheon of misterios shared with Vodu Dominicano (Las 21 Divisiones). The baile de palos is a couple dance of 'respect,' traditionally danced unembraced; spirit possession may occur (English Wikipedia; Mediatheque Caraibe/Lameca).
card.insight: Ethnomusicologists Josue Santana and Edis Sanchez note the palos drums are considered sacred and are even 'baptized' before use - underscoring that this is a religious, not merely recreational, tradition.
card.image_significance: Sacred long-drum dance of respect. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Dominican Republic.
